clinical_study.brief_title: AI Feedback for NIH Grant Proposal Development (GRANT-AI)
clinical_study.official_title: Grant Review and Adaptive Navigation Using Transformers and AI (GRANT-AI): A Pilot Randomized Trial of Large Language Model Versus Retrieval-Augmented Generation Feedback for NIH Proposal Development

resp_party.investigator_title: Professor and Chair, Department of Surgery

brief_summary.textblock: GRANT-AI is a pilot randomized trial testing whether artificial intelligence feedback helps investigators develop NIH grant proposals. Participants preparing an NIH proposal in clinical, translational or health services research are randomized 1:1 to receive structured feedback on their proposal sections from either a large language model aligned to NIH review criteria, or a retrieval-augmented generation system grounded in a curated corpus of funded proposals, reviewer summary statements and institutional guidance. Participants in both arms also receive written critique from an experienced NIH reviewer. The trial assesses feasibility, acceptability and preliminary performance signals in order to inform a future full-scale trial. It is not powered for a formal comparison of the two feedback systems.

detailed_description.textblock:
Participants submit three core NIH proposal sections (Specific Aims, Significance/Innovation, and Approach) within a 90-day window, receive feedback from their assigned system and from an expert reviewer, and revise and resubmit iteratively. Both platforms carry behavioral engagement features including progress tracking and peer comparison. A purposive subsample is invited to a semi-structured interview after the quantitative phase. Primary outcomes are feasibility indicators: recruitment yield, timely submission of all three sections within the 90-day window, and blinded reviewer ratings of section quality on a 1-9 NIH-style scale. Secondary and exploratory outcomes include AI-derived quality metrics, responsiveness to feedback, proposal submission rates and, where available, NIH peer review outcomes.
This record is a retrospective registration. The study received an exempt determination from the University of South Florida Institutional Review Board on 18 September 2025 and enrolled its first participant on 7 January 2026. Enrollment did not reach the planned sample of 30.

clinical_study.why_stopped: Enrollment rate insufficient to reach the planned sample size

primary_outcome.outcome_measure: Recruitment yield: number of institutions approached and proportion yielding at least one enrolled participant
primary_outcome.outcome_time_frame: Through study completion, up to 12 months

outcome_description.textblock: Count of institutions and departments approached, proportion producing a named eligible contact, and proportion producing an enrolled participant.

primary_outcome.outcome_measure: Proportion of participants submitting all three core proposal sections within the 90-day window

outcome_description.textblock: Specific Aims, Significance/Innovation and Approach. Participants not submitting all three within the window are classified as non-completers.

primary_outcome.outcome_measure: Quality of submitted proposal sections rated by blinded independent reviewers

outcome_description.textblock: Section-specific NIH-style criteria scored on a 1-9 scale (1 = exceptional, 9 = poor) by reviewers blinded to arm and with no role in delivering feedback.

secondary_outcome.outcome_time_frame: Through study completion, up to 90 days

outcome_description.textblock: Number of feedback cycles completed and time between feedback delivery and resubmission.
Whether the participant submitted a proposal, recorded as a binary event and as time to submission.

secondary_outcome.outcome_measure: NIH peer review outcome where available

outcome_description.textblock: Impact score, percentile rank, discussion status and funding decision.
Five-point Likert items on motivation, confidence and usefulness of feedback, plus open-ended responses.

arm_group_description.textblock: Structured written feedback on each submitted proposal section generated by a large language model aligned to NIH review criteria and tailored to the funding announcement, delivered alongside written critique from an experienced NIH reviewer.

Structured written feedback on each submitted proposal section generated by a retrieval-augmented generation system grounded in a curated corpus of funded NIH proposals, reviewer summary statements and institutional guidance, delivered alongside written critique from an experienced NIH reviewer.

intervention_description.textblock: Automated section-level feedback aligned to NIH review criteria, delivered through the study platform with behavioral engagement features including progress tracking and peer comparison.

Automated section-level feedback grounded in a retrieved corpus of funded proposals and reviewer summary statements, delivered through the study platform with behavioral engagement features including progress tracking and peer comparison.

criteria.textblock:
Inclusion Criteria: - Early-career (within 10 years of terminal degree), mid-career (10-20 years) or senior investigator (more than 20 years, or holding a tenured or institutional leadership position) - Based in a clinical department in the United States - Actively developing an NIH research grant proposal in clinical research, translational science or health services research - Proposal involves direct human data collection or analysis, such as clinical trials, observational studies, registries, electronic health records or patient-reported outcomes - Able to provide electronic informed consent
Exclusion Criteria: - Proposals focused exclusively on animal models, preclinical systems or basic science - Proposals targeting non-NIH funding mechanisms

ipd_description.textblock: De-identified operational data and analysis code supporting the start-up feasibility report are archived at https://github.com/ricardopietrobon/grant-ai . Institution identity is replaced by a salted surrogate; personal names and addresses are removed.
